claims.text: Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 requires temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has relatively high porosity.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 has a relatively high tendency for damage in corrosive plating conditions.
SPS at approximately 2000 °C and approximately 50 MPa will produce fully densified ZrB2.
ZrB2 prepared by the proposed SPS treatment will remain single-phase.
The proposed SPS treatment will produce less porosity than conventional sintering above 2300 °C.
Rapid SPS processing reduces grain growth.
Accelerated particle bonding during SPS minimizes porosity.
Pulsed current in SPS promotes rapid diffusion and densification at lower temperatures.
Applied uniaxial pressure during SPS promotes rapid diffusion and densification at lower temperatures.
Lower porosity provides fewer nucleation sites for damage during prolonged exposure to a corrosive liquid plating bath.
Reducing pore-mediated damage will enhance the mechanical integrity of ZrB2 during plating-bath exposure.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will develop fewer holes during long-duration liquid plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will experience fewer component failures during long-duration liquid plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Non-uniform temperature distributions during SPS could cause local material inhomogeneities.

contradictions.description: The proposed SPS temperature is approximately 2000 °C, while the preparation boundary is stated as temperature greater than 2000 °C; a run at exactly 2000 °C would fall outside the stated boundary.
